title: Span resolution mini playbook
content:
Quick notes to self about tricky span-resolution + cleanup heuristics. Purpose: keep a short, practical reference for ad-hoc decisions while I batch-clean the small-payments dataset. Not formal, will move to shared drive when stable.

High-level goal:
- Consistent entity spans for downstream NER/rule-based extractors. Avoid both over-splitting and over-joining. Prefer minimal consistent spans that still map to canonical values.

Current pain points observed:
1) Dates with modifiers: "early 2019", "Q3 2020", "late-July 21" -> sometimes labeled as DATE, sometimes as FREE_TEXT. Decision: label entire phrase as DATE when it contains at least one temporal token (year, quarter, month) and optional modifier (early/late/approx). Examples: "early 2019" -> DATE, "Q3 2020" -> DATE, "late-July 21" -> DATE.

2) Contract amounts mixed with currency symbols and words: "USD 5k", "$5,000 per month". Rule: include adjacent rate words if they change meaning (per month, per year). So "$5,000 per month" -> AMOUNT span includes "per month". But "$5k sign-on" -> AMOUNT is just "$5k" ("sign-on" is context).

3) Hyphenated model names vs phrase splits: "end-to-end" should usually be a single TECH term if referring to model behaviour; otherwise split. Use heuristics: if hyphenated term appears in our model catalog or docs, keep as single span. Otherwise, prefer split unless meaning clearly atomic.

4) Nested spans: e.g., "John Doe (CFO)" where "John Doe" labelled PERSON and "CFO" as TITLE. Keep both but annotate outer-highest priority in the primary label column and nested in secondary column. For small-batch jobs we don't create nested labels in tools, so instead add a note in NOTES column: "PERSON: John Doe; ROLE: CFO".

Concrete labeling examples (samples to copy into tool):
- Input: "Invoice dated early 2019 for USD 5,000 per quarter"
  - DATE: "early 2019"
  - AMOUNT: "USD 5,000 per quarter" (include frequency)

- Input: "Payment to Acme-Logistics scheduled Q3 2020"
  - ORG: "Acme-Logistics" (treat hyphenated org names as single span)
  - DATE: "Q3 2020"

- Input: "Refund (pro-rated) $125"
  - AMOUNT: "$125"
  - NOTES: "pro-rated kept in NOTES, not part of AMOUNT span"

Unclear/edge rules I keep flipping on (notes):
- Round numbers with units attached, e.g., "5k" vs "5,000": normalize downstream but label raw text as-is. TODO: add column for normalized_amount in future exports.
- Percent ranges: "10-15%" -> label as PERCENT and prefer whole span (keep dash).
- Phone numbers in free text (no international prefix): label PHONE when pattern matches >= 7 digits contiguous, but exclude invoice numbers that happen to be numeric if preceded by "INV" or "Invoice#".

Cleanup heuristics during batch passes (these are scripts I use manually):
- Step 1: run small regexp to unify whitespace and remove zero-width chars.
- Step 2: unify common contractions in company names ("Co" -> "Co."?) Wait: don't force punctuation. Instead add mapping table and use only for normalization field.
- Step 3: flag spans containing slashes ("20/04/2020", "ACME/LLC") for manual review because tool sometimes splits on slash.

Quick manual QA checklist (what I scan for before finalizing a batch):
- Are date modifiers consistently included?
- Are currency tokens attached to correct numeric span? (no stray "USD" left out)
- Are hyphenated orgs and tech names kept atomic?
- Any accidental nested entities flattened? Add note if so.

Open questions for the labeling group (for sync):
- Do we want to standardize that frequency words (per month/annually) are always part of AMOUNT spans across datasets? I think yes for finance domain but might be noisy for others.
- How should we surface nested labels in the export format? Current workaround (NOTES col) is ugly. Proposal: two-level label columns (LABEL, SUB_LABEL) in CSV export.

Todo (short-term):
- [ ] Add 15 curated examples for ambiguous hyphenation cases (e.g., "Acme-Logistics", "end-to-end", "co-op").
- [ ] Draft small markdown doc and move this playbook to shared_drives/data-quality when stable. Link to DL-442.
- [ ] Add regex to flag phone/invoice confusion and push to manual queue.

Notes-to-self: keep entries short, when in doubt pick the smaller atomic span that preserves easy mapping to canonical id. Document any exceptions inline in NOTES column rather than trying to memorize.

Appendix: quick sample rows I paste into the tool for testing (CSV-like, but here inline):

"Invoice #1234","Invoice dated early 2019 for USD 5,000 per quarter","DATE:early 2019; AMOUNT:USD 5,000 per quarter"
"Refund","Refund (pro-rated) $125","AMOUNT:$125; NOTES:pro-rated kept separately"
"Client","Payment to Acme-Logistics scheduled Q3 2020","ORG:Acme-Logistics; DATE:Q3 2020"

End of scratchpad. Small, practical, will iterate. If I don't move this by end of month, ping me (nora).
